thread:
maria: Kicking off us-east3-alpha provisioning. First nodegroup failed during coldstart, looks like ENI quota + kernel driver mismatch. Anyone on call?
aj: Seeing the same. bootstrap.sh failed while building nvidia driver on our custom AMD-optimized AMI. Log excerpt: ```make[2]: *** No rule to make target 'nvidia.ko'```
infra-cicd: deploy-bot: terraform apply ERROR -> CreatingNetworkInterface: You have reached the maximum number of network interfaces for your account in the region. (RequestID: req-78a) :cry:
kevin: @maria can you paste the full bootstrap log? also which AMI id?
maria: AMI: rwinf-us-east3-alpha-ami-20260511. Full tail: ```[  123.456] nvidia: loading out-of-tree module taints kernel. error: Unknown symbol nv_p2p_map_sg````
anya: That nv_p2p error smells like driver/kernel version mismatch. We rolled a kernel bump in the AMI build two days ago. Did the image get promoted accidentally?
aj: Confirmed. Image build pipeline promoted a canary AMI with kernel 6.4 and the nvidia module we ship is compiled for 6.1. CI didn't catch it because no GPU nodes in canary.
kevin: ENI quota is independent issue though. Cloud console shows account-level ENI limit exhausted in us-east3. We have orphaned interfaces from failed spot allocations.
sre-oncall: Oncall ack. Opening cloud support ticket for ENI quota and purging stale ENIs in parallel. ETA 2h for quota increase.
maria: Short-term runbook suggestion: 1) fallback to previous AMI (kernel 6.1) 2) reclaim ENIs by draining/terminating stale spot instances 3) re-run bootstrap. Thoughts?
aj: Works for me. How quick to revert AMI? image-id: rwinf-us-east3-ami-stable-20260401 exists. We can patch launch template to point to it and re-run nodegroup create.
kevin: Reclaiming ENIs: I'll run a script to find unattached ENIs with our tag and release. Might free ~30/200 we need. Command I'll run: ```aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=tag:stack,Values=rw-alpha --query 'NetworkInterfaces[?Status==`available`].NetworkInterfaceId'```
anya: Also add an extra validation step to boot flow: check kernel/nvidia module version pair before starting model runtime. Fail fast if mismatch.
maria: Agreed. Add to bootstrap: ```/opt/bin/check-driver.sh || exit 1```
infra-cicd: deploy-bot: updated launch template for us-east3-alpha -> image rwinf-us-east3-ami-stable-20260401 (by aj). Triggering nodegroup create.
aj: nodegroup create started. Watching cloud-init logs.
kevin: ENI cleanup freed 28 interfaces, still short ~10. Sre-oncall engaged cloud support for temporary quota bump.
sre-oncall: cloud support created case #CS-91234. Provider granted temporary +50 ENI for 3 hours.
maria: Nodegroup bootstrapped successfully on fallback AMI. kubelet registered. Running validation: kube-dns, kube-proxy, gpu plugin, runtime smoke.
anya: Smoke test: launching 10 parallel inference requests against a small quantized model. Observed 95ms median latency, no OOM. Good.
aj: Rolling handoff checklist: - AMI pinned - validation green - node labels correct (gpu=rtx-a6000) - taints applied - capacity targets met (min 4, target 12)
maria: Note: we should add an automated AMI-driver compatibility test in image pipeline to avoid this. Filing a small task.
kevin: Cost note: using fallback AMI keeps instance runtime same but we used extra capacity to reprovision; incremental cost ~ $1.2k for the temporary nodes + spot churn. Logging in cost channel.
sre-oncall: Handoff to infra ops at 21:00 UTC. Leaving ticket open until we have stable AMI promotion and driver test.
maria: Thanks all. Marking this thread resolved for now, followups: AMI compatibility test, bootstrap driver check, ENI quota preflight for future regions. :thumbsup:
